kpis.label: Net Income
kpis.note: Continuing operations. Net income attributable to shareholders (incl. discontinued Reebok-era items) was €1,340m in FY2025.

charts.title: Revenue by Region
charts.annotation: Regions shown are Europe, North America, Greater China and Latin America -- Emerging Markets and Japan/South Korea are disclosed but not yet captured as columns. Wholesale is a channel cut across all regions, not an additional region, so it is plotted as a line rather than stacked.

charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income
Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Adidas AG: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Adidas AG: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Adidas AG: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Adidas AG: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Adidas AG: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on. Lease principal repaid (store leases under IFRS 16) was €643m in FY2025, the largest single deduction between reported FCF and owner FCF.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF -- FY2025 operating cash flow fell to €751m from €2,910m in FY2024 as inventories rose 17% to fund growth

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Adidas AG: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Adidas AG: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

regionRevenue.title: Revenue by region
regionRevenue.content:
Adidas reports net sales by geographic segment: Europe, North America, Greater China, Latin America, plus Emerging Markets and Japan/South Korea (not separately charted here). Wholesale is the revenue sold through third-party retail partners, overlaid as a line across all regions rather than stacked with them.

For Adidas AG: the turnaround story is regional as much as it is group-level -- Greater China is rebuilding after the 2021-2022 boycott-driven slump, while North America remains the laggard among the major regions even as Europe and Latin America post double-digit currency-neutral growth.

What to watch:

  • Greater China's growth trend as a read on the post-boycott recovery
  • North America versus the other regions -- is the gap closing
  • Wholesale growth relative to total revenue growth as a proxy for the DTC/e-commerce mix shift management targets

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Adidas AG: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Adidas AG: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Adidas AG: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
